lesson.subtitle: Lesson 11 -- Have You Ever?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Catarina | Lesson 11 -- Have You Ever?

listenings.text: So, my teacher asked us to write a bucket list, and I thought, okay, easy. Then I started, and I realized I have never done most of the things I want to do. I have never seen snow. Not once, in my whole life. I have been to the beach about a hundred times, so that one does not count. I have never tried sushi, and my friends say that is a crime. And the scary one: I have never been on a really big roller coaster. I went on a small one twice, when I was nine, and I screamed the whole time. So, number one on the list? The big one. I want to be brave about it. Ask me again next year.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the science museum. Before we start, a quick question. Has anyone here ever been inside a planetarium? Hands up. Okay, three of you. So most of you have never seen one, and today is going to be unforgettable. So far, you have only seen the entrance. In the next two hours you will see the dome, the moon rocks, and the earthquake room. Some people find the earthquake room a little scary, so if you do not want to go in, you do not have to. And one rule: please do not touch the moon rocks. They have been to space. You have not.

items.situation: A new classmate seems interesting. Ask her two questions about her experiences.
Your teacher asks: Have you ever eaten something really strange? Answer, and add one detail.
Someone says: I went skydiving last summer! Ask three follow-up questions.
Tell me one thing from your bucket list, and say why you have never done it.
A friend asks: Have you ever been on a roller coaster? You have, twice. Answer, then ask back.
